messages:
maya: Pushed a small TF change to map instance types -> capacity reservation + spot fallback for the GPU nodepools. Asking for a quick secrets wiring and tfvars sanity check before I merge. PR: https://git.redwood.ai/r/redwood/infrastructure/pulls/482

maya: TL;DR: we want g5.* as preferred, fall back to p4d if not available in AZ, and attach the capacityReservation id when using reserved nodes. Also moved the cloud-init secret reference from SSM to KMS-encrypted S3 (per security request).

maya: Relevant snippet from modules/gpu-nodepool/variables.tf added: 
```hcl
variable "instance_map" {
  type = map(object({
    priority = number
    instance_types = list(string)
    capacity_reservation_id = optional(string)
    allow_spot = bool
  }))
}
```

maya: Example tfvars I pushed: 
```hcl
instance_map = {
  primary = { priority = 0, instance_types = ["g5.2xlarge","g5.xlarge"], capacity_reservation_id = "cr-0a1b2c3d", allow_spot = false }
  fallback = { priority = 10, instance_types = ["p4d.24xlarge"], capacity_reservation_id = "", allow_spot = true }
}
```

sam: Quick look — this shape makes sense. Couple questions: 1) capacity_reservation_id sometimes empty string vs null? 2) How does ASG/cluster autoscaler pick the fallback set?

maya: @sam good q. I used empty string for TF module because we want to avoid null in lists, and the module checks length > 0 to attach. Autoscaler logic: nodegroup creation tries priorities in order; we create separate nodegroups per map key (priority 0, priority 10). Autoscaler can scale each, and we rely on scheduling and taints to prefer the primary. If primary can't schedule due to capacity, fallback nodegroup can scale (we also set maxSurge and burst reserve).

leo: For secrets: you moved cloud-init from SSM param to s3+kms. Who owns the KMS key and do we have IAM role changes in the nodepool? Also need to ensure node bootstrap reads the S3 object — that's new userdata.

maya: Ownership: security owns the KMS key (alias: alias/redwood/gpu-nodepool). I added an iam instance-profile role policy in module: s3:GetObject for arn:aws:s3:::redwood-gpu-init/* and kms:Decrypt for that KMS alias. Diff in PR shows the policy.

leo: Please paste the IAM snippet here for quick eyeball.

maya: 
```json
{
  "Effect": "Allow",
  "Action": ["s3:GetObject"],
  "Resource": ["arn:aws:s3:::redwood-gpu-init/*"]
}
{
  "Effect": "Allow",
  "Action": ["kms:Decrypt"],
  "Resource": ["arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111122223333:key/abcd-efgh-1234"]
}
```

sam: That looks fine. Two operational asks before merge: 1) run terraform plan in staging and paste the nodegroup naming to make sure we don't accidentally create duplicate groups across AZs; 2) add a quick preflight CI job that validates the KMS alias exists (we had a typo once).

maya: Plan output attached to PR; nodegroup names are suffixed with cluster and priority so uniqueness is preserved. I'll add the KMS check to CI in a follow-up, or put a minimal validation script in this PR if you prefer.

devx-ci: ci/build: terraform fmt & validate passed. ci/plan: ran in staging; shows two nodegroups to be created: redwood-gpu-primary-0 (desired=2) and redwood-gpu-fallback-10 (desired=0).

leo: Minor nit: for allow_spot = true on fallback, ensure we set node taints to tolerate spot preemption (so critical pods don't land there). Also add a label e.g., node.kubernetes.io/spot=true so we can route lower-priority workloads.

maya: Good call. I added tolerations + label for fallback. Snippet in module node taints: 
```yaml
nodeSelector:
  node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: "fallback"
labels:
  redwood/gpu-tier: "fallback"
taints:
  - key: "spot"
    value: "true"
    effect: "NoSchedule"
```

sam: LGTM overall. One more ops ask: can we add a rollback policy in the module to remove capacityReservation reference if creation fails? I don't want stuck allocations.

maya: There's a module-level var rollback_on_error = true defaulting to true. If the reservation attach fails, module attempts to create the nodegroup without the CR id. I added logs to the module to surface that in plan/apply.

leo: Awesome. I'm +1 for merge after you add the KMS existence check (small script) and run a second plan with updated labels/taints.

maya: Will do. Thanks everyone — I'll push a tiny CI check and re-run plan, then merge. @sam @leo please glance at PR if you have 5 mins. :slightly_smiling_face:

ops-bot: Scheduled maintenance window conflict detected: GPU capacity reservation cr-0a1b2c3d has an existing allocation during 2026-04-02 02:00-03:00 UTC. If you rely on that CR, consider changing AZ or timing.

maya: Thanks ops-bot — we'll move the apply window to 2026-04-02 05:00 UTC to avoid conflict.

sam: ACK, thanks for the heads up.

leo: Approved conditional on CI KMS check and second plan.

maya: Putting the KMS check in now and will ping when plan is green.
